modules.remaining: Native callback server binds the requested TCP address and retains a shared result/error identity. Route/state validation precedes claimed/settled rejection; only the first valid code invokes completion. Duplicate parameters retain their first value, plus is replaced before percent decoding, malformed escapes remain literal and UTF-8 decoding follows URLSearchParams replacement. Completion errors render the source 502 page and propagate the original cause. Cancel leaves a claimed completion running; abort/timeout/close settle the wait without canceling the active exchange, which still returns its success/failure page. Close drains active HTTP handlers. Manual input has its own cancellation context, cancels an unclaimed browser wait and is aborted on exit. Callback rejection precedes manual rejection; after a successful callback wait an already-observed manual failure wins, while successful manual input cannot replace a claimed browser result. Undefined callback completion falls back to manual input; explicit null remains a callback result. Native option/callback mutation requires caller synchronization. Exact JS microtask ordering versus blocking Go prompt invocation, abort during bind/listener-registration, platform-specific bind errors, malformed request targets/callback values and exhaustive HTTP/timer/abort scheduling remain unproven. OpenRouter now uses this server and manual-input helper in full native login flows.
